There is no ack timeout. If the client's decode promise rejects (a worker 'error' message) or resolves null, dispatchFrames sends no ack. The server's check_frame_acknowledgment_status then stays False forever and the UI stream freezes until the socket reconnects. FreeMoCap's relay, by contrast, has an ack-lag reset and catches IndexError.

An upper bound on the UI rate can be derived from the code (it is not an end-to-end measurement). Each payload cycle takes at least one 10.2-10.4 ms sleep plus the synchronous build: about 12.8-17.5 ms plus 2.3-2.8 ms SHM copy at 5x1080p, or 3.5-8.9 ms plus 0.9-4.9 ms at 5x720p. That caps 5x1080p at about 1/(10.3+15.1..20.3 ms), roughly 33-39 Hz, before RTT, rAF-gated decode and the extra skipped poll. 5x720p is about 50-70 Hz under the same assumptions. With the build on the event loop, a 60 Hz UI at 5x1080p is not reachable as written.

The UI build runs in the same process and on the same CPUs as the camera processes' MJPEG retrieve and VideoWriter.write. OpenCV in this venv reports getNumThreads() = 28, and skellycam never calls cv2.setNumThreads, so the server-side resize can fan out across all cores. Its effect on capture and disk-write timing at 5x60 fps is unmeasured.

The module-global _reusable_bytes_payload is shared by every camera group and every websocket connection (including FreeMoCap's camera-only relay). Correctness today depends on the bytearray[:n] slice copy. Removing that copy with a memoryview would require per-group and per-connection buffers.

Writer-side avoidable copy that feeds the UI tap: put_data assigns copy(data) into the slot. That is a full-frame temporary (0.87 ms at 1080p) plus the slot write, on every frame in every camera process.

Version difference: the skellycam source in FreeMoCap's venv matches 23ccbf20 (same git tree da98850e; diff --strip-trailing-cr is empty for websocket_server.py, frontend_payload_bytearray.py, camera_group.py, ring_buffer_shared_memory.py, camera_group_shared_memory.py and opencv_camera_loop.py). The transport stack differs: FreeMoCap's venv has uvicorn 0.51.0 (auto selects WebSocketsSansIOProtocol), websockets 16.1.1 and starlette 1.3.1. SkellyCam's venv has uvicorn 0.44.0 (legacy WebSocketProtocol), websockets 16.0 and starlette 1.0.0.

While the Playback tab is open, stream_video (a sync def, run in the threadpool of the server process) may transcode a non-web-compatible recording to H.264 with pyav/libx264 before serving it. That is CPU-heavy work in the same process as the UI tap, and could coincide with capture if playback is opened during a session.

corrected_flow_steps.action: grab/retrieve into the process-local frame_rec_array; put_frame(overwrite=True), which copies (copy(data)) and then writes the slot and bumps last_written_index; THEN handle_video_recording writes the same local array to cv2.VideoWriter synchronously (the disk path never reads SHM)
await asyncio.sleep(0.01); if last ack >= last_sent (and the previous poll was not un-acked), call CGM.get_latest_frontend_payloads synchronously; if_newer_than is ignored
target = min(last_written_index); per camera, the lap check and then np.copyto of the slot into cached recarrays; verify the frame numbers agree (ValueError otherwise)
per camera: optional full-res rotate, resize 0.5, imencode q60, tobytes, copy into the module-global bytearray; footer; return a slice copy

acquire _send_lock; starlette send_bytes; uvicorn legacy WebSocketProtocol send, then write_frame and Frame.serialize (one BytesIO copy, plus zlib if permessage-deflate is negotiated); Proactor transport.write; drain
store the ArrayBuffer in pendingPayloadRef, overwriting any older one
if not paused and idle, transfer the ArrayBuffer to the decode worker and await the result; the next rAF is scheduled only after it completes
parse headers; sequentially per camera: Blob, then createImageBitmap; post the bitmaps back as transferables (or an 'error' message, which means no ack downstream)
update per-camera fps; transfer each bitmap to that camera's OffscreenCanvas worker; send JSON ack {type:'frameAcknowledgment', frameNumber: max}
corrected_flow_steps.to: Per-camera OffscreenCanvas worker and FastAPI server (ack)

corrected_flow_steps.action: resize the canvas if needed; keep the newest bitmap; on the worker's rAF, transferFromImageBitmap into the bitmaprenderer context

websocket.receive; json.loads; set last_received_frontend_confirmation (unvalidated type) and _display_image_sizes (always None from skellycam-ui); reply pong to ping; any exception sets global_kill_flag
corrected_flow_steps.to: image relay task (unblocks next payload) / camera processes (if killed)

risk_verdicts.risk: An unexpected exception in any UI websocket task sets global_kill_flag. Every camera loop then exits (ipc.should_continue) and finalizes, truncating any recording in progress. Triggers include a malformed '{'/'[' text message from any client (ValueError), a non-numeric frameNumber in an ack (TypeError in the relay, inferred from the code), and the cross-camera mismatch ValueError or IndexError from get_latest_multiframe (unlikely given lockstep grabbing). A display or client problem can therefore end a disk recording.

The conclusion stands but the reasoning was wrong. A slow or absent UI cannot block the writer. The reason is not that 'the UI does not advance last_read_index, which keeps the overwrite check intact': no production consumer advances last_read_index, and the writer uses overwrite=True. The real reason is that disk writes happen in the camera process from its local recarray, before and independent of any SHM reader. The UI's remaining couplings to disk are the kill flag and CPU contention.

The SHM copy, resize, JPEG encode and (if negotiated) zlib deflate all run synchronously on the single uvicorn event loop, about 15-27 ms per multiframe at 5x1080p from the measured components (2.3-2.8 copy + 12.8-17.5 build in the bench, 7.1 in the profiler, + up to 6.7 deflate). HTTP control endpoints, websocket receive and the other tasks are blocked meanwhile. Derived bound: a UI at 5x1080p cannot reach 60 Hz (at most about 33-39 Hz before RTT); 5x720p reaches at most about 50-70 Hz. End-to-end rates were not measured.

Display throughput is cut by several latencies in series: stop-and-wait (one payload in flight per ack), a 10 ms poll plus an extra skipped poll after any un-acked check, rAF-gated serial decode, and an ack only after decode. The UI rate is set by the round trip and the display refresh, not by camera fps.
There is no ack timeout. One failed decode, a null result or a lost ack stalls the SkellyCam UI stream permanently until reconnect.
if_newer_than is ignored, so after a fast ack the server can re-encode and re-send a frame the client already has. That wastes encode time on the event loop and inflates the client's display fps.
Logs at TRACE and above, framerate, state and frames share one send lock and one socket, so heavy logging competes with frames for the loop and the socket. The size of the effect is unmeasured.

The server-side encode shares CPUs with capture and synchronous VideoWriter.write in the camera processes. OpenCV may use 28 threads for resize because setNumThreads is never called. The impact on 5x60 fps capture and disk timing is unmeasured.

Every UI payload copies all raw full-res frames out of SHM (about 31 MB per multiframe at 5x1080p, about 1.9 GB/s at a 60 Hz UI) just to make 960x540 thumbnails. Each JPEG is then copied twice (tobytes, assemble), the whole payload twice more (slice, BytesIO in serialize; a third time in the Proactor buffer if a write is pending), and probably once more in the browser Blob (spec-level, unmeasured). The writer side adds one more full-frame temporary per frame (copy(data) in put_data).
The client never sends displayImageSizes, so small tiles still receive full 0.5-scale images. That means more resize and encode work and more bytes than needed.

map.area: SkellyCam -> FreeMoCap handoff and FreeMoCap UI tap
map.summary: FreeMoCap runs SkellyCam inside its own FastAPI/uvicorn process. It shares SkellyCam's singleton CameraGroupManager, mounts SkellyCam's camera router under /skellycam, and drives recording and config with direct Python calls, not HTTP. Images cross from SkellyCam into FreeMoCap only through SkellyCam's per-camera shared-memory ring buffers. The ring-buffer DTO (the shared-memory names) is pickled to each worker, and each worker attaches by name. Each worker then copies the frame it wants out of shared memory with get_data_by_index (np.copyto). That is random access by frame number, it never advances last_read_index, so the writer cannot see these readers and overwrites freely. With the default config (centralized GPU inference, charuco on) each processed multiframe is copied 3N times at full resolution: once per camera in N CameraNode processes, N times in the SkeletonInferenceNode, and N times in the main process for the UI, where get_images_by_frame_number also allocates fresh recarrays on every call. The aggregator reads no pixels, only the write index. Keypoints and observations flow onward as pickled metadata through a main-process pubsub relay. The UI gets JPEG images (re-encoded in the main process on the asyncio thread) plus a separate binary keypoints message and a JSON overlay payload, all over one websocket. The realtime pipeline's frame rate is tied to that websocket's ack loop: the aggregator's result_consumed_event is set only by the websocket relay. The installed SkellyCam (777b058c) is content-identical to SkellyCam HEAD 23ccbf20, so there are no version differences in this area.

claims.statement: FreeMoCap's venv runs skellycam 2.0.0a6 from git commit 777b058c (requested branch main). The git tree of 777b058c is byte-identical to SkellyCam HEAD 23ccbf20 (both tree da98850e; 777b058c is a merge whose second parent is 23ccbf20). All 142 installed .py files match 777b058c once CRLF line endings are ignored, so every line number below is valid for both versions. Reproduce: sh C:/Users/Dom/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/c--Users-Dom-GitHub-freemocap-skellycam/ad23e4da-d956-400c-b95c-1c7166f96ad9/scratchpad/verify_installed_skellycam_matches.sh (output saved alongside as verify_installed_skellycam_matches.out.txt).

SkellyCam is embedded in-process. freemocap/__main__.py creates one global_kill_flag and a skellycam WorkerRegistry in PROCESS mode, then runs one uvicorn server. create_fastapi_app builds FreemocapApplication, which takes SkellyCam's module-level singleton CameraGroupManager via get_or_create_camera_group_manager. SkellyCam's camera_router is mounted under the /skellycam prefix of the same app, so FreeMoCap code and SkellyCam HTTP routes share the same CameraGroup objects.

FreeMoCap does not mount SkellyCam's websocket server. It serves its own WebsocketServer at /websocket/connect and imports only ServerFramerateCalculator from skellycam.api.websocket. The UI connects to ws://host:port/websocket/connect.

How a camera group and pipeline are created: POST /freemocap/realtime/apply calls FreemocapApplication.create_or_update_realtime_pipeline, which calls CameraGroupManager.create_or_update_camera_group. CameraGroup.start awaits the extracted configs, creates CameraGroupSharedMemory in the main process with read_only=True, and publishes its DTO to the camera workers. RealtimePipelineManager.create_pipeline then builds and starts the pipeline. If a pipeline already exists, any later call only pushes a config update and returns (freemocap_application.py L100-102).

Realtime pipeline topology: one CameraNode worker per pipeline camera, one RealtimeSkeletonInferenceNode (only when use_centralized_inference and skeleton tracking are on), one RealtimeAggregatorNode, and one CharucoRecorderNode when charuco is on. Defaults are worker_mode=PROCESS, charuco on, skeleton on, detector rtmpose and use_centralized_inference=True, so the default for N cameras is N+3 extra OS processes alongside SkellyCam's camera processes.

The shared-memory handoff passes names, not pixels. RealtimePipeline passes camera_group.shm.to_dto(), whose per-camera SharedMemoryRingBufferDTO holds the shm names, dtype and shape, as worker kwargs. In the child, SharedMemoryElement.recreate calls shared_memory.SharedMemory(name=...) and wraps shm.buf in an np.recarray. FreeMoCap workers therefore map the same physical ring buffers that SkellyCam's camera processes write, and attaching copies nothing.

The aggregator never touches pixels. It attaches the group shm read-only and reads only latest_multiframe_number, the minimum of last_written_index across cameras. It publishes a ProcessFrameNumberMessage(frame_number=that value), both as a bootstrap/fallback (L445-458) and optimistically right after collecting frame N's camera outputs (L569-581). This is 'latest' sampling: any frames written between requests are skipped by the realtime pipeline.

Every FreeMoCap image read goes through SharedMemoryRingBuffer.get_data_by_index: random access by index, not get_next_data or get_latest_data. It never updates last_read_index (confirmed: the value stays -1 after reads), so FreeMoCap readers are invisible to the writer's _check_for_overwrite. SkellyCam's camera loop writes with overwrite=True in any case. FreeMoCap therefore cannot back-pressure capture; a lagging reader instead gets IndexError (lapped) or a frame-number mismatch.

Each CameraNode copies its camera's full frame (metadata plus HxWx3 uint8) from shared memory into a process-local recarray with np.copyto. The recarray is allocated once and reused (frame_recarray = None, then passed back each iteration). frame_recarray.image[0] is a view of that local copy, not of shared memory. When rotation != -1, cv2.rotate makes another full-size copy. Confirmed with np.shares_memory: result vs SHM slot is False, image[0] vs local recarray is True, rotate output vs input is False. Reproduce: C:/Users/Dom/GitHub/freemocap/freemocap/.venv/Scripts/python.exe -I C:/Users/Dom/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/c--Users-Dom-GitHub-freemocap-skellycam/ad23e4da-d956-400c-b95c-1c7166f96ad9/scratchpad/fmc_handoff_copy_semantics.py

A CameraNode copies the frame out of shared memory for every ProcessFrameNumber request, whether or not it has a tracker. In centralized mode with charuco disabled, skeleton_tracker and charuco_tracker are both None, yet the node still does the get_data_by_index copy (and rotate) and publishes an output with no observations.

The centralized RealtimeSkeletonInferenceNode, a single process, drains its ProcessFrameNumber subscription down to the newest request, dropping stale ones. It then reads the same frame number from all N camera ring buffers in a sequential loop with get_data_by_index into per-camera reusable recarrays. That is N more full-frame copies on top of the CameraNodes' N, plus conditional cv2.rotate copies, before tracker.process_batch. It maps each camera's shm twice: once via CameraGroupSharedMemory.recreate, used only for .valid, and once via per-camera recreate.

Frame-integrity checks after the copy: CameraNode raises RuntimeError on a camera-ID mismatch and only warns on a frame-number mismatch ('possible ring buffer overwrite'). The skeleton node warns and uses the frame anyway. get_data_by_index checks for staleness before np.copyto but not after, so a slot overwritten during the copy (a reader lapped mid-copy) is caught only by these after-the-fact frame-number checks. The aggregator raises RuntimeError ('WRONG FRAME') if a camera output's frame_number differs from the requested one.

No image ever travels over FreeMoCap's pubsub. CameraNodeOutputMessage carries only camera_id, frame_number and the charuco/skeleton Observation objects. Every topic uses a multiprocessing.Queue publication queue that a main-process PubSubRelay thread polls (1 ms sleep when idle) and fans out to per-subscriber multiprocessing.Queues (maxsize 100, evicting the oldest when full). Each child-to-child message is therefore pickled and unpickled twice, through two pipes, and can wait up to about 1 ms in the relay at each hop.

How results flow onward: the aggregator collects one CameraNodeOutputMessage per camera for the requested frame. In GPU mode it also waits for the matching SkeletonInferenceResultMessage, keyed by frame_number, and splices the per-camera skeletons into the camera outputs. It then triangulates and filters, and publishes AggregationNodeOutputMessage (camera outputs, filtered keypoints_arrays, rigidified skeleton, CoM, XCoM, body kinematics) on AggregationNodeOutputTopic, which the main process subscribes to. The CharucoRecorderNode subscribes to CameraNodeOutputTopic as well.

The realtime pipeline's throughput is gated by the UI websocket. The aggregator requests a new frame only while result_consumed_event is set (L450-452), and clears it each time it publishes (L830-831). The only code that sets it again is RealtimePipeline.get_latest_frontend_payload (L476-477). That function is called only by the websocket image relay, through RealtimePipelineManager and FreemocapApplication, and only after the previous frame has been acked by the browser (or the lag reaches 300). With no websocket client connected the aggregator therefore stops after its first one or two frames. (This is read from the code; no test was run to show it.)

The browser acks images as soon as they arrive, not after decoding. handleMessage reads frame_number from bytes 8-15 of each binary image payload and stores the payload as 'pending', so the newest payload wins. On the next requestAnimationFrame it sends {frameNumber, displayImageSizes}. Only one decode is in flight at a time (processingFrameRef). The server stores the ack and the display sizes, which set the JPEG resize target.

What the UI receives: per packet, the websocket relay sends (a) a msgspec JSON FrontendPayload with 2D charuco/skeleton overlays, CoM, XCoM and kinematics, (b) a binary keypoints message, and (c) the binary multi-camera JPEG image payload, serialized by an asyncio.Lock on one websocket. The UI gets both images and keypoints, and both come from the main FreeMoCap process.

UI image tap in realtime mode: the main process calls skellycam CameraGroup.get_frontend_payload_by_frame_number(aggregation_output.frame_number), so the displayed image is the exact frame the keypoints were computed on. That calls CameraGroupSharedMemory.get_images_by_frame_number, whose module-level _frame_recarray_cache is never written. Every call therefore allocates N new frame-sized recarrays and np.copyto's each full frame out of shared memory. Measured: a new recarray on each call, cache size 0. Cost was 0.42 ms per camera at 720p and 0.88 ms at 1080p (median, alloc plus copy).

create_frontend_payload, run in the main process for each camera, works in this order: an optional cv2.rotate (full-size copy), cv2.resize down to at most 0.5 scale or the UI display box, cv2.imencode JPEG at quality 60, jpeg_data.tobytes() (copy), a copy into the module-level _reusable_bytes_payload, and finally _reusable_bytes_payload[:current_pos], a bytearray slice that is a new copy of the whole payload (confirmed: shares_memory False). Measured with a single random-noise camera (worst case for JPEG): 1.9 ms at 720p and 3.5 ms at 1080p, median.

The image readout, JPEG encoding and keypoint serialization run synchronously inside the async _frontend_image_relay coroutine, which calls the plain function self._app.get_latest_frontend_payloads without to_thread. They therefore block the uvicorn asyncio event loop that also serves the HTTP control routes, such as recording start/stop. Only the wait on result_ready_event is moved off the loop, with asyncio.to_thread.

Camera-only mode (no live realtime pipeline): FreemocapApplication falls back to SkellyCam's CameraGroupManager.get_latest_frontend_payloads, then CameraGroup.get_latest_frontend_payload, then get_latest_multiframe. That path reads the minimum write index, copies it into instance-cached recarrays (_latest_frames, reused) and JPEG-encodes it. CameraGroup.get_latest_frontend_payload ignores its if_newer_than argument, and wait_for_any_result_ready falls back to a 10 ms sleep when no pipeline is alive.

The binary keypoints message is built in the main process from AggregationNodeOutputMessage by build_keypoints_payload, which allocates a bytearray. It is built on every realtime packet: no environment-variable gate exists in the source, so the FREEMOCAP_BINARY_KEYPOINTS comment in frontend_payload.py is stale. Its message-type bytes 3/4/5 deliberately avoid SkellyCam's image bytes 0/1/2 so the browser can tell the two apart from the first byte.

Browser image path: the ArrayBuffer is transferred zero-copy to one decode Web Worker. That worker decodes every camera's JPEG with pure-JS jpeg-js on the CPU, inside one worker, and copies each RGBA result with ArrayBuffer.slice. The buffers are transferred to the main thread and then to per-camera offscreen-renderer workers, which wrap them in ImageData and call createImageBitmap (the GPU upload).

Recording control from FreeMoCap to SkellyCam is a direct in-process call, not HTTP. The /freemocap/calibration/recording/start|stop and /freemocap/mocap/recording/start|stop routes call FreemocapApplication.start_recording_all / stop_recording_all, which call CameraGroupManager.start_recording_all_groups / stop_recording_all_groups. CameraGroup.start_recording pauses the cameras (await_paused=True), sets the orchestrator's first_recording_frame_number to max frame_count+3, publishes RecordingInfoMessage on SkellyCam's pubsub, and unpauses. stop_recording mirrors this with last_recording_frame_number and then awaits RecordingFinishedMessage from every camera.

Camera config changes reach SkellyCam through CameraGroup.update_camera_settings. It publishes UpdateCamerasSettingsMessage on SkellyCam's pubsub and polls every 100 ms until each camera returns a DeviceExtractedConfigMessage. FreeMoCap triggers it via CameraGroupManager.create_or_update_camera_group (from realtime/apply) or RealtimePipeline.update_camera_configs.

The FreeMoCap UI also calls SkellyCam's own HTTP routes, served by the same process: /skellycam/camera/group/apply, /group/all/record/start, /group/all/record/stop, /group/all/pause_unpause and /detect. It calls /freemocap/realtime/apply for the pipeline and /freemocap/{calibration,mocap}/recording/* for recordings that start posthoc processing. The UI also lists /skellycam/camera/update, but SkellyCam's camera_router defines no such route.

During a calibration recording, FreeMoCap publishes CalibrationRecordingStateMessage(is_active=True) to each live pipeline and switches it to charuco-only mode. Switching publishes a PipelineConfigUpdate, which makes every CameraNode rebuild its charuco tracker and shuts down the SkeletonInferenceNode process synchronously inside the route handler. The CharucoRecorderNode caches only observations for frames the aggregator requested, so cache coverage is bounded by the UI-gated rate in H15.

Failure coupling: RealtimePipeline builds its PipelineIPC from camera_group.ipc.global_kill_flag, which is the same flag SkellyCam's CameraGroupIPC.should_continue checks. Any exception in a CameraNode, the aggregator (including the 'WRONG FRAME' RuntimeError) or the SkeletonInferenceNode calls ipc.kill_everything(), which sets that flag. SkellyCam's camera loops then exit 'while ipc.should_continue' and close the recorder in their finally block, ending any in-progress recording.

FreeMoCap readers are not on the disk-write path. The camera process copies its process-local frame_rec_array into shared memory (put_frame) first, then hands that same local array to VideoRecorder.record_frame. The video writer never reads the ring buffer, so FreeMoCap's shared-memory reads cannot stall or corrupt a disk write. They can only compete with it for CPU and memory bandwidth (see H28 for the kill-flag coupling).

Ring-buffer depth: each camera gets a 1 GiB ring by default (memory_allocation=ONE_GIGABYTE; from_config passes no length). Measured: 388 slots of 2.64 MiB at 1280x720x3 (6.47 s at 60 fps) and 172 slots of 5.93 MiB at 1920x1080x3 (2.87 s at 60 fps), about 5 GiB of shared memory for 5 cameras. A FreeMoCap reader more than one ring-length behind gets IndexError, which the websocket relay catches and handles by resetting last_sent_frame_number.

Posthoc pipelines do not use the ring buffer. Each VideoNode (one per camera) opens the recorded file with cv2.VideoCapture(path, CAP_FFMPEG) and calls read() in sequence; read() is called without an output array, so each call returns a decoded frame. It runs the tracker and publishes only VideoNodeOutputMessage(observation) on an unbounded VideoNodeOutputTopic. When annotation is on, it also re-encodes frames with cv2.VideoWriter.

Both packages enable beartype.claw.beartype_this_package() at import time, so hot-path functions are wrapped in runtime type checkers. The probe's traceback shows create_frontend_payload running inside an @beartype wrapper. The per-call cost of these checks has not been measured.

Copy count per processed multiframe with the default config (N cameras, centralized inference, charuco on): 3N full-resolution copies out of shared memory (N in CameraNodes, N in the SkeletonInferenceNode, N in the main process for the UI). Up to 3N more full-size cv2.rotate copies happen when rotation is set. In the UI branch the main process adds N frame-sized allocations, N downscales, N JPEG encodes, N copies of each JPEG (tobytes) plus N into the reusable buffer, and one whole-payload slice copy. With per-camera inference (use_centralized_inference=False) the count drops to 2N.

FreeMoCap passes the camera frame_number as get_data_by_index's 'apparent index'. That index counts writes (last_written_index + 1 on each put_data). Correctness therefore depends on frame_number equalling the write count for every camera, and a mismatch triggers only the warnings or raise in H12. The docstring itself tells callers to verify the frame number after reading.

Existing test harness that could be used for benchmarks: freemocap/tests/pipelines/mocks/mock_camera_group.py builds the real CameraGroupSharedMemory and put_frame()s recorded-video frames with overwrite=True. The realtime pipeline then runs unmodified against real shared memory, which makes it a ready harness for end-to-end handoff benchmarks without cameras.

frame_copies.where: FreeMoCap CameraNode process (one per camera): get_data_by_index into the reusable frame_recarray
frame_copies.necessary: Not strictly needed. Charuco and skeleton trackers only need a read-only HxWx3 view. A view of the SHM slot plus a seqlock/frame-number re-check after processing would avoid it. It also runs when the node has no tracker at all (centralized mode, charuco off). Measured 0.094 ms (720p) and 0.217 ms (1080p) median, hot-cache lower bound.

frame_copies.where: FreeMoCap CameraNode: cv2.rotate when camera_info.rotation != -1
frame_copies.necessary: Needed only if the tracker cannot take rotated coordinates. Rotating keypoints instead of pixels would avoid it. Measured 0.75 ms (720p) and 1.91 ms (1080p) median.

frame_copies.where: FreeMoCap SkeletonInferenceNode: _read_frames does get_data_by_index for each of N cameras, sequentially
frame_copies.kind: memcpy (np.copyto, SHM to process-local) x N
frame_copies.necessary: Duplicates the CameraNode copies of the same frames. The batch could be built from SHM views directly, or straight into the model's input tensor during resize/normalize.

frame_copies.where: FreeMoCap SkeletonInferenceNode: cv2.rotate per camera when rotated
frame_copies.necessary: Same as the CameraNode rotate; could be merged into the inference preprocessing warp.

frame_copies.where: SkellyCam (called by FreeMoCap main process): CameraGroupSharedMemory.get_images_by_frame_number allocates a new recarray per camera and copies into it
frame_copies.necessary: The allocation is a defect: _frame_recarray_cache is never populated. The copy is avoidable because the next step only reads the image to downscale it, and resize can read the SHM view directly. Measured 0.42 ms (720p) and 0.88 ms (1080p) per camera.

frame_copies.where: SkellyCam create_frontend_payload (FreeMoCap main process): cv2.rotate when rotated
frame_copies.necessary: Avoidable: rotate after the downscale, or let the browser rotate.

frame_copies.where: SkellyCam create_frontend_payload: cv2.resize (scale <= 0.5) then cv2.imencode JPEG q60
frame_copies.kind: encode (a reduced-size image is created first)
frame_copies.necessary: Needed for bandwidth to the browser as long as JPEG is the wire format. It runs on the asyncio thread of the main process. Measured 1.9 ms (720p) and 3.5 ms (1080p) per camera on random noise.

frame_copies.where: SkellyCam create_frontend_payload: jpeg_data.tobytes(), copy into _reusable_bytes_payload, then _reusable_bytes_payload[:current_pos]
frame_copies.kind: memcpy (compressed bytes) x2 per camera, plus a whole-payload slice copy
frame_copies.necessary: Avoidable: cv2.imencode's output buffer could be written directly, and a memoryview could be returned instead of a slice. The slice copy was confirmed with np.shares_memory False. These copies are small (about 67-150 KB per camera in the test).

frame_copies.where: FreeMoCap websocket relay: websocket.send_bytes(images_bytearray) through starlette, uvicorn and websockets 16.1.1
frame_copies.necessary: Needed to reach the Electron UI. Whether the websockets library copies the payload again when framing has not been verified (open question).

frame_copies.where: FreeMoCap UI decode worker: jpeg-js decode, then raw.data.buffer.slice for each camera
frame_copies.necessary: The decode is needed for JPEG. The slice copy could be avoided by transferring raw.data.buffer directly when byteOffset is 0. The later postMessage transfers are zero-copy.

frame_copies.where: FreeMoCap UI per-camera offscreen worker: new ImageData(new Uint8ClampedArray(pixelBuffer)) then createImageBitmap

risks_for_priorities.risk: Any exception in a FreeMoCap realtime node (including the aggregator's 'WRONG FRAME' RuntimeError on a frame-number mismatch, and CameraNode's camera-ID mismatch) calls kill_everything(). That sets the global_kill_flag SkellyCam's camera loops check, which ends capture and any in-progress recording. A failure in display or analysis code can therefore stop disk writes.

FreeMoCap's realtime workers (3N full-frame copies per processed frame, charuco/RTMPose inference, JPEG encoding) run on the same machine as SkellyCam's capture and encode processes, with no CPU or memory-bandwidth isolation or priority. Contention could slow the camera loop's VideoRecorder.record_frame. Whether this causes dropped frames on disk has not been measured.

Recording start/stop HTTP handlers share the asyncio event loop with the websocket relay, which runs N-camera SHM copies and JPEG encodes synchronously (about 4.4 ms per 1080p camera by the probe: 0.88 ms copy plus 3.5 ms encode). A stop or start command can wait behind an encode cycle. CameraGroup.start_recording and stop_recording also pause the cameras around the transition by design.

Realtime pipeline throughput is capped by the UI. A new frame is requested only after the websocket relay consumes the previous result, which in turn waits for the browser's rAF-paced ack. The pipeline therefore cannot exceed the UI display or ack rate, and with no UI client it stalls.

Every control/result hop goes child -> mp.Queue -> main-process relay thread (1 ms idle poll) -> mp.Queue -> child, pickling twice. One processed frame needs ProcessFrameNumber, N CameraNodeOutputs, a SkeletonInferenceResult and an AggregationNodeOutput, so several milliseconds of relay latency stack up serially. The relay thread also competes for the GIL with the asyncio loop doing JPEG work.

At 1080p the 1 GiB ring holds 172 slots, 2.87 s at 60 fps. A FreeMoCap reader that falls further behind gets IndexError or torn/mismatched frames, because the staleness check happens only before the copy.

The UI image path does serial per-camera work on one thread at each end: main-process JPEG encoding of all N cameras on the asyncio thread, and browser jpeg-js decoding of all N cameras in a single worker. With 5 cameras that is N x (copy + resize + encode) per UI frame on one Python thread.

3N full-resolution copies out of shared memory per processed multiframe in the default centralized config: N CameraNode copies (made even without a tracker), N more in the SkeletonInferenceNode for the same frames, and N in the main process for the UI. Rotations add up to 3N more.

get_images_by_frame_number allocates a fresh full-frame recarray per camera on every UI payload, because the module cache it checks is never filled. That puts a 6 MB allocation per 1080p camera per UI frame on the main process.

claim_verdicts.final_statement: SkellyCam runs inside the FreeMoCap process. freemocap/__main__.py creates one global_kill_flag and a SkellyCam WorkerRegistry in PROCESS mode, then runs one uvicorn server. create_fastapi_app calls create_freemocap_app, which builds FreemocapApplication with SkellyCam's module-level singleton CameraGroupManager (get_or_create_camera_group_manager). SkellyCam's camera_router is mounted under /skellycam on the same app, and its handlers call the same singleton, so FreeMoCap code and SkellyCam HTTP routes share the same CameraGroup objects.

FreeMoCap does not mount SkellyCam's websocket server. It serves its own WebsocketServer at /websocket/connect, and the only import it takes from skellycam.api.websocket is ServerFramerateCalculator. The UI connects to ws://host:port/websocket/connect (default port 53117).

POST /freemocap/realtime/apply calls FreemocapApplication.create_or_update_realtime_pipeline. If any pipeline already exists, it pushes only a pipeline-config update to the first pipeline and returns (L100-102), and the request's camera_configs are ignored. Otherwise it calls CameraGroupManager.create_or_update_camera_group. For a new group, CameraGroup.start awaits the extracted configs, creates CameraGroupSharedMemory in the main process with read_only=True, and publishes the DTO to the camera workers. RealtimePipelineManager.create_pipeline then builds and starts the pipeline.

The realtime pipeline has one CameraNode per pipeline camera. It adds one RealtimeSkeletonInferenceNode only when use_centralized_inference and skeleton tracking are both on, one RealtimeAggregatorNode, and one CharucoRecorderNode when charuco is on. The defaults are worker_mode=PROCESS, charuco on, skeleton on, detector rtmpose and use_centralized_inference=True. FreeMoCap's WorkerRegistry is PROCESS mode, so N cameras give N+3 FreeMoCap worker processes alongside SkellyCam's camera processes. log_pipeline_times also defaults to True.

The handoff passes shared-memory names, not pixels. RealtimePipeline passes camera_group.shm.to_dto() as worker kwargs. Each per-camera SharedMemoryRingBufferDTO holds the shm names, dtype and shape. In the child, SharedMemoryElement.recreate calls shared_memory.SharedMemory(name=...) and wraps shm.buf in an np.recarray, so FreeMoCap workers map the same physical ring buffers that SkellyCam's camera processes write, and attaching copies nothing. Note that CameraNode attaches with read_only=False (see missed facts).

The aggregator reads no pixels. It attaches the group shm read-only and reads only latest_multiframe_number, the minimum of last_written_index across cameras. It publishes ProcessFrameNumberMessage(frame_number=that value) in two places: in a bootstrap/fallback block (L445-458), and optimistically right after it has collected all camera outputs for frame N (L569-581). This is 'latest' sampling, so the realtime pipeline skips any frames written between requests.

Every FreeMoCap image read goes through SharedMemoryRingBuffer.get_data_by_index, which is random access by index; FreeMoCap never calls get_next_data or get_latest_data. get_data_by_index never updates last_read_index (it stays -1 after reads), so FreeMoCap readers are invisible to the writer's _check_for_overwrite. SkellyCam's camera loop writes with overwrite=True in any case. FreeMoCap therefore cannot back-pressure capture. A lagging reader gets IndexError (lapped) or a frame-number mismatch instead.
claim_verdicts.note: grep across freemocap/ and the installed skellycam finds get_data_by_index at camera_node.py L256 and realtime_skeleton_inference_node.py L403, plus skellycam's own camera_group_shared_memory.py L134/L155, which the main-process UI path uses.

claim_verdicts.final_statement: Each CameraNode copies its camera's full frame (metadata plus HxWx3 uint8) from shared memory into a process-local recarray with np.copyto. The recarray is allocated on the first read (frame_recarray = None at L188) and reused after that. frame_recarray.image[0] is a view of that local copy, not of shared memory. When rotation != -1, cv2.rotate makes another full-size copy. np.shares_memory confirms all three: the result vs the SHM slot is False, image[0] vs the local recarray is True, and the rotate output vs its input is False.

A CameraNode copies the frame out of shared memory (and rotates it) for every ProcessFrameNumber request, before it checks whether it has a tracker. In centralized mode with charuco disabled, skeleton_tracker and charuco_tracker are both None, yet the node still does the get_data_by_index copy and publishes an output with no observations.

The centralized RealtimeSkeletonInferenceNode is a single process. It sleeps wait_1ms() at the top of every loop and drains its ProcessFrameNumber subscription to the newest request, dropping stale ones. It then reads that frame number from all N camera ring buffers in a sequential loop, using get_data_by_index into reusable per-camera recarrays. These are N more full-frame copies on top of the CameraNodes' N, plus conditional cv2.rotate copies, before tracker.process_batch. Read exceptions are caught and the camera is skipped. Each camera's shm is mapped twice: once via CameraGroupSharedMemory.recreate, used only for .valid, and once via a per-camera recreate.

Frame-integrity checks after the copy. CameraNode raises RuntimeError on a camera-ID mismatch. On a frame-number mismatch it only warns, but it then publishes actual_frame_number (the slot's frame number). The aggregator raises RuntimeError 'WRONG FRAME' for any camera output whose frame_number differs from the requested one, and that calls kill_everything(). So a CameraNode mismatch is effectively fatal to the whole app. The skeleton node warns and still publishes the batch under requested_frame_number, so it can silently mix frames. get_data_by_index checks staleness before np.copyto but not after. Its bound check (head - index >= len raises) also still accepts index = head - (len - 1), which is exactly the slot the writer will overwrite next (off-by-one). A torn read of the oldest accepted slot is therefore possible, and only the after-the-fact frame-number checks can catch it.

claim_verdicts.final_statement: No image travels over FreeMoCap's pubsub. CameraNodeOutputMessage carries only camera_id, frame_number and the charuco/skeleton Observation objects. Every topic has a multiprocessing.Queue publication queue (maxsize 100, and child put() blocks when it is full). A non-daemon PubSubRelay thread in the main process polls all of them, sleeping 1 ms when idle, and fans out with put_nowait to per-subscriber multiprocessing.Queues (maxsize 100), evicting the oldest message when a queue is full. A child-to-child message is therefore pickled and unpickled twice, through two pipes, and can wait up to about 1 ms in the relay at each hop.

The aggregator collects one CameraNodeOutputMessage per camera for the requested frame. In centralized GPU mode it also waits for the matching SkeletonInferenceResultMessage, keyed by frame_number. It gives up after _SKELETON_RESULT_WAIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 2.0 s and proceeds without it. It splices the per-camera skeletons into the camera outputs, then triangulates and filters. It publishes AggregationNodeOutputMessage on AggregationNodeOutputTopic, which the main process subscribes to. The message holds the camera outputs, filtered keypoints_arrays, rigidified skeleton, CoM, XCoM and body kinematics, plus the full pipeline_config on every frame. The CharucoRecorderNode also subscribes to CameraNodeOutputTopic.

The realtime pipeline is NOT generally gated by the UI websocket. result_consumed_event is checked in exactly one place, the bootstrap/fallback request (L450-452). The optimistic request after camera outputs are collected (L573-581) does not check it. The comment at L570-571 says the event is 'guaranteed set' there, but that holds only for the first frame: after the first publish clears the event (L830), the next frame was itself requested optimistically, without any check. So as long as the shm write index has advanced past the last request when outputs are collected, which is the normal case when the pipeline is slower than capture (e.g. RTMPose at 5x60 fps), the aggregator free-runs with no websocket client at all. The gate only bites when the pipeline is faster than capture (latest_shm_frame == latest_requested_frame at L576). Then the next request waits in the bootstrap path until RealtimePipeline.get_latest_frontend_payload sets result_consumed_event (L476-477). That function is the only production setter; the test driver realtime_driver.py L64-65 also sets it. When the aggregator free-runs, outputs pile up in the main-process AggregationNodeOutputTopic subscription (maxsize 100, the relay evicts the oldest), and the websocket relay drains it to the latest (L462-466). This is read from code; a run could not be made (see missed facts: the FreeMoCap venv cannot import the realtime pipeline).

claim_verdicts.final_statement: The browser acks images on arrival, not after decoding. handleMessage reads frame_number from bytes 8-15 of each binary image payload. That offset is correct because SkellyCam's header dtype is align=True, so the i8 lands at offset 8. It stores the payload as 'pending', so the newest payload wins. On the next requestAnimationFrame it sends {type:'frameAcknowledgment', frameNumber, displayImageSizes}. processingFrameRef keeps one decode in flight at a time. The server stores the ack and the display sizes, which set the JPEG resize target.

For each packet, the websocket relay sends (a) a msgspec JSON FrontendPayload with 2D charuco/skeleton overlays, CoM, XCoM and kinematics, (b) a binary keypoints message, and (c) the binary multi-camera JPEG image payload. All three go over one websocket, and each send takes an asyncio.Lock separately, so log or app-state messages can interleave between them. The UI gets both images and keypoints, and both come from the main FreeMoCap process.

In realtime mode the main process calls SkellyCam's CameraGroup.get_frontend_payload_by_frame_number(aggregation_output.frame_number), so the displayed image is the exact frame the keypoints were computed on. That calls CameraGroupSharedMemory.get_images_by_frame_number. Its module-level _frame_recarray_cache is never written anywhere, so every call allocates N new frame-sized recarrays and np.copyto's each full frame out of shared memory. Measured: a new recarray on every call, cache size 0. Median cost per camera (alloc plus copy) was 0.42 ms at 720p and 0.88 ms at 1080p.
claim_verdicts.note: grep finds _frame_recarray_cache only at L17 (definition), L149 (key check) and L152 (read); it is never assigned.

claim_verdicts.final_statement: create_frontend_payload runs in the main process for each camera, in this order: an optional cv2.rotate (full-size copy); cv2.resize down to at most 0.5 scale or the UI display box (a new array each call); cv2.imencode JPEG at quality 60; jpeg_data.tobytes() (a copy); a copy into the module-level _reusable_bytes_payload; and finally _reusable_bytes_payload[:current_pos], a bytearray slice that copies the whole payload again (shares_memory False). Median timings for one random-noise camera, the worst case for JPEG: 1.9 ms at 720p and 3.5 ms at 1080p.

The image readout, JPEG encoding and keypoint serialization run synchronously inside the async _frontend_image_relay coroutine. It calls the plain function self._app.get_latest_frontend_payloads without to_thread, and RealtimePipelineManager takes a multiprocessing.Lock inside it. This work therefore blocks the uvicorn asyncio event loop, which also serves the HTTP control routes such as recording start/stop. Only the wait on result_ready_event is moved off the loop, via asyncio.to_thread.

Camera-only mode (no live realtime pipeline): FreemocapApplication falls back to SkellyCam's CameraGroupManager.get_latest_frontend_payloads, then CameraGroup.get_latest_frontend_payload, then get_latest_multiframe. That path reads the minimum write index, copies the frames into instance-cached recarrays (_latest_frames, reused) and JPEG-encodes them. CameraGroup.get_latest_frontend_payload ignores its if_newer_than argument, and wait_for_any_result_ready falls back to a 10 ms sleep when no pipeline is alive. The same frame is therefore re-copied, re-encoded and re-sent on every acked loop whenever the UI rAF/ack rate exceeds the capture rate.
claim_verdicts.note: The duplicate-resend consequence is read from code: the relay sends whatever is latest after each ack, and nothing compares it with last_sent_frame_number.

claim_verdicts.final_statement: The binary keypoints message is built in the main process from AggregationNodeOutputMessage by build_keypoints_payload. That function is in freemocap/core/viz/frontend_keypoints_serializer.py, not binary_keypoints_protocol.py, and it allocates a fresh bytearray(total_size) per call. It is built on every realtime packet. No FREEMOCAP_BINARY_KEYPOINTS gate exists in the .py sources (only stale .pyc files contain the string), so the comment in frontend_payload.py L71 is stale. Its message-type bytes 3/4/5 deliberately avoid SkellyCam's image bytes 0/1/2, so the browser can demultiplex on the first byte (isKeypointsMessage checks byte 0 == 3).

Browser image path. The ArrayBuffer is transferred zero-copy to one decode Web Worker. That worker decodes every camera's JPEG with pure-JS jpeg-js on the CPU. The decode call is synchronous, so the Promise.all over cameras runs them one after another in one worker. It copies each RGBA result with ArrayBuffer.slice. The buffers are transferred to the main thread and then to per-camera offscreen-renderer workers, which wrap them in ImageData (a view, no copy) and call createImageBitmap. Calling createImageBitmap 'the GPU upload' comes from a code comment; whether it uploads to the GPU or makes another CPU copy has not been verified.

Recording control from FreeMoCap to SkellyCam is a direct in-process call, not HTTP. The /freemocap/calibration/recording/start|stop and /freemocap/mocap/recording/start|stop routes call FreemocapApplication.start_recording_all / stop_recording_all, which call CameraGroupManager.start_recording_all_groups / stop_recording_all_groups. CameraGroup.start_recording pauses the cameras (await_paused=True), sets the orchestrator's first_recording_frame_number to max frame_count + 3, publishes RecordingInfoMessage on SkellyCam's pubsub, optionally starts audio, and unpauses. stop_recording mirrors this with last_recording_frame_number, then awaits a RecordingFinishedMessage from every camera (100 ms poll) and finalizes.

Camera config changes reach SkellyCam through CameraGroup.update_camera_settings. It publishes UpdateCamerasSettingsMessage on SkellyCam's pubsub and polls every 100 ms until each camera returns a DeviceExtractedConfigMessage. In practice the FreeMoCap UI triggers it through SkellyCam's own route POST /skellycam/camera/group/apply (cameras-thunks.ts L146), which calls CameraGroupManager.create_or_update_camera_group. /freemocap/realtime/apply reaches create_or_update_camera_group only when no pipeline exists yet. RealtimePipeline.update_camera_configs is defined but has no callers in freemocap/.
claim_verdicts.note: grep 'update_camera_configs|update_camera_settings' in freemocap/ finds only the definition and its body (realtime_pipeline.py L423-424).

claim_verdicts.final_statement: The FreeMoCap UI also calls SkellyCam's own HTTP routes, served by the same process: /skellycam/camera/detect, /group/apply, /group/all/pause_unpause, and (via recording-thunks.ts) /group/all/record/start and /group/all/record/stop. The record routes bypass FreeMoCap's posthoc launch. The UI calls /freemocap/realtime/apply for the pipeline and /freemocap/{calibration,mocap}/recording/* for recordings that start posthoc processing. server-urls.ts also lists /skellycam/camera/update (updateConfigs), but SkellyCam's camera_router defines no such route and no UI code uses that endpoint, so it is dead.

During a calibration recording, FreeMoCap publishes CalibrationRecordingStateMessage(is_active=True) to each live pipeline and switches it to charuco-only mode. Switching publishes a PipelineConfigUpdate, which makes every CameraNode rebuild its charuco tracker. It also calls SkeletonInferenceNode.shutdown() synchronously inside the async route handler: a join of up to 3 s, then terminate plus 3 s, then kill plus 2 s, all on the event loop. The CharucoRecorderNode caches observations only for frames the aggregator requested. In charuco-only mode the pipeline is normally faster than capture, so requests fall back to the gated bootstrap path (H15), and the cache rate is then bounded by how fast the websocket relay consumes results. When the pipeline is slower than capture, the cache rate is bounded by pipeline speed instead.

Failure coupling: RealtimePipeline builds its PipelineIPC from camera_group.ipc.global_kill_flag, which is the same flag SkellyCam's CameraGroupIPC.should_continue checks. Any exception in a CameraNode, the aggregator (including 'WRONG FRAME') or the SkeletonInferenceNode calls ipc.kill_everything(), which sets that flag. SkellyCam's camera loops then leave 'while ipc.should_continue' and call finish_recording in their finally block, ending any in-progress recording. In addition, SkellyCam's WorkerRegistry child monitor sends SIGTERM to the whole server process whenever the flag is set (see missed facts).

FreeMoCap readers are not on the disk-write data path. The camera process copies its process-local frame_rec_array into shared memory (put_frame) and then passes that same local array to VideoRecorder.record_frame, which writes frame.image[0] (or a rotated copy) to cv2.VideoWriter. The video writer never reads the ring buffer, so FreeMoCap's shared-memory reads cannot stall or corrupt a disk write's pixels. They can only compete with it for CPU and memory bandwidth, and they can stop it through the kill flag (H28).

Each camera gets a 1 GiB ring by default (memory_allocation=ONE_GIGABYTE; from_config passes no length). That is 388 slots of 2.64 MiB at 1280x720x3 (6.47 s at 60 fps) and 172 slots of 5.93 MiB at 1920x1080x3 (2.87 s at 60 fps), about 5 GiB of shared memory for 5 cameras. What happens to a reader that falls a ring-length behind depends on the reader. The main-process UI read raises IndexError, which the websocket relay catches by resetting last_sent_frame_number. The SkeletonInferenceNode catches it and skips that camera. The CameraNode does NOT catch it: get_data_by_index at L256 sits inside the try whose except calls ipc.kill_everything(), so a lapped CameraNode ends capture and any recording.

Posthoc pipelines do not use the ring buffer. Each VideoNode (one per camera) opens the recorded file with cv2.VideoCapture(path, CAP_FFMPEG) and calls read() in sequence, without an output array, so each call returns a newly decoded frame. It runs the tracker (or reuses cached realtime charuco observations) and publishes only VideoNodeOutputMessage(observation) on VideoNodeOutputTopic, which is unbounded (queue_maxsize=0). With annotation on, it also re-encodes frames with cv2.VideoWriter.

Both packages call beartype.claw.beartype_this_package() at import time, so hot-path functions are wrapped in runtime type checkers. The probe's traceback shows create_frontend_payload running inside an @beartype wrapper. The per-call cost has not been measured.

Full-resolution copies out of shared memory in the default config (N cameras, centralized inference, charuco on): 2N for every frame the pipeline processes (N in the CameraNodes, made even with no tracker, plus N in the SkeletonInferenceNode for the same frames), plus N in the main process for every frame the UI is actually sent. Because the aggregator free-runs (H15) and the relay drains to the latest output, the UI copies happen at the websocket send rate, which can be lower than the processing rate. So 3N per processed multiframe is an upper bound, not the norm. Rotation adds up to one full-size cv2.rotate per copy site. The UI branch also allocates N fresh frame-sized recarrays, makes N downscales (new arrays), N JPEG encodes, N tobytes copies, N copies into the reusable buffer, and one whole-payload slice copy. With use_centralized_inference=False the count drops to N per processed frame plus N per UI frame. Separately, SkellyCam's writer makes one avoidable extra full-frame copy per write (put_data copy(data); see missed facts).

FreeMoCap passes the camera frame_number as get_data_by_index's 'apparent index', and that index counts writes (last_written_index + 1 on each put_data). Correctness therefore depends on frame_number equalling the write count for every camera. A mismatch triggers only the checks in H12, where the CameraNode path ends in the aggregator's fatal 'WRONG FRAME'. The docstring itself tells callers to verify the frame number after reading.

freemocap/tests/pipelines/mocks/mock_camera_group.py builds the real CameraGroupSharedMemory (read_only=False) and put_frame()s recorded-video frames with overwrite=True, so the realtime pipeline runs unmodified against real shared memory. As shipped, it is a correctness harness, not a throughput harness. drive_realtime_lockstep writes one frame, waits for its output and then sets result_consumed_event, so it never exercises the free-running, latest-sampling behaviour. A throughput benchmark needs a free-running writer at the target fps. It also cannot run in the current FreeMoCap venv, because importing freemocap.core.pipeline.realtime.realtime_pipeline fails on a skellytracker version mismatch.

P1: A lapped CameraNode kills capture and recording. get_data_by_index raises IndexError when head - index >= ring length, and CameraNode does not catch it. Its outer except calls ipc.kill_everything(), which sets the shared global_kill_flag. A CameraNode can lag that far, for example, if a pending ProcessFrameNumber request is older than 2.87 s at 1080p while the node rebuilds trackers on a config update (camera_node.py L196-241) or builds a per-camera ONNX session before entering its loop (L170-177, use_centralized_inference=False). The SkeletonInferenceNode, by contrast, catches read errors (L407-412).

P1: A CameraNode frame-number mismatch, which only logs a warning there, becomes fatal downstream. The node publishes actual_frame_number, the aggregator raises 'WRONG FRAME' when it differs from latest_requested_frame, and that triggers kill_everything(). A torn or overwritten slot read in any CameraNode therefore ends the recording.

Off-by-one in SkellyCam's staleness check. get_data_by_index raises only when head - index >= ring_buffer_length, so it accepts index = head - (len-1), whose slot ((head+1) % len) is the next one the writer overwrites. Readers of the oldest accepted frame can therefore race the writer with no detection before the copy. Probe: ring length 5, head 9, get_data_by_index(5) is accepted, and slot 0 == next write slot 0.

P1: SkellyCam's WorkerRegistry child monitor, which FreeMoCap shares (__main__.py L58-62), calls os.kill(os.getpid(), SIGTERM) on the whole FreeMoCap server process in two cases: any worker exits with a non-zero code without being marked intentionally terminated, or global_kill_flag becomes set for any reason. A crash in any FreeMoCap realtime node, including a native crash that never raises in Python, therefore takes down the entire app, including SkellyCam capture and any in-progress recording.

P1: Every FreeMoCap websocket task sets global_kill_flag = True on any unexpected exception: the app-state sender, the image relay, the log relay and the client message handler. For example, a client text message that starts with '{' but is not valid JSON raises ValueError (L402-403), which reaches the handler's except and kills the whole app, recordings included. A UI-side bug can therefore stop disk writes.

CameraNode attaches the SkellyCam ring with read_only=False. SkellyCam's read_only is only a Python flag that gates put_data/get_next_data; the SharedMemory mapping is always writable. The probe wrote through a read_only=True mapping and the writer saw the change (7 -> 123). Any FreeMoCap process can therefore corrupt the frames the UI and other readers see. Disk writes are not affected, because VideoRecorder writes the camera's local array (H29).

A zero-copy read path is available. ring_shm.buffer[slot].image is a view of shared memory (np.shares_memory True), and cv2.resize and cv2.imencode accept it directly. All three main-process UI copies and the reader copies could be replaced by views plus a post-use frame-number re-check (seqlock-style).

The writer side of the handoff makes an unnecessary extra full-frame copy. SkellyCam's put_data does ring_shm.buffer[slot] = copy(data), which allocates and copies the frame and then copies it again into SHM. Measured median: buf[i] = copy(frame) took 0.546 ms (720p) and 1.243 ms (1080p), against 0.073/0.159 ms for a single np.copyto. That is about 7-8x the cost of the necessary copy, on every frame of every camera. Event-loop blocking in control routes. BaseNode.start does time.sleep(0.25) per node on Windows (_SPAWN_STAGGER_SECONDS), and RealtimePipelineManager.create_pipeline / pipeline.start() run synchronously inside the async /freemocap/realtime/apply handler. That blocks the uvicorn loop, and with it the websocket relay and every other route, for about (N+3) x 0.25 s, plus the BaseNode.shutdown joins (up to 3 s + 3 s + 2 s) when update_config restarts or stops the SkeletonInferenceNode. The calibration start route does exactly that right after it has started recording.

After a skeleton toggle or detector swap, the SkeletonInferenceNode is recreated with camera_ids=self.camera_group.camera_ids (every camera in the group) instead of the pipeline's realtime camera subset. When realtime_camera_ids is a subset, the restarted node then copies frames and runs inference for cameras the pipeline does not use.

Main-process throughput cost of a free-running aggregator. Every AggregationNodeOutputMessage carries the full RealtimePipelineConfig plus all per-camera Observations. It is unpickled and re-pickled by the PubSubRelay thread, and when the queue is full an older one is unpickled again to be evicted. The websocket relay then unpickles every queued message on the asyncio thread just to keep the last one (get_nowait loop). All of this competes for the GIL with JPEG encoding in the main process.

The camera process records synchronously. The SkellyCam camera loop calls put_frame and then VideoRecorder.record_frame (cv2.VideoWriter.write) inline before grabbing the next frame. CPU contention from FreeMoCap workers on the same machine therefore slows the capture-and-write loop directly; no queue absorbs it. Whether this causes dropped frames at 5x60 fps is unmeasured.

risk_verdicts.risk: Any exception in a FreeMoCap realtime node calls kill_everything(). That includes the aggregator's 'WRONG FRAME' (which a CameraNode frame-number mismatch triggers), a CameraNode camera-ID mismatch, and an uncaught IndexError in a lapped CameraNode. kill_everything sets the global_kill_flag that SkellyCam's camera loops check, ending capture and any in-progress recording. SkellyCam's WorkerRegistry monitor then SIGTERMs the whole server process. A worker dying with a non-zero exit code (no Python exception needed), or an exception in any websocket relay task, has the same effect. So a failure in display or analysis code can stop disk writes.

FreeMoCap's realtime workers run on the same machine as SkellyCam's capture-and-encode processes, with no CPU or memory-bandwidth isolation or priority. Their load is 2N full-frame SHM copies per processed frame plus N per UI frame, charuco and RTMPose inference, and main-process JPEG encoding. The camera loop writes to disk synchronously (VideoRecorder.record_frame inline), so contention slows capture directly. Whether this drops frames on disk at 5x60 fps has not been measured.

The recording start/stop HTTP handlers share the asyncio event loop with the websocket relay, which runs the N-camera SHM copies and JPEG encodes synchronously (about 4.4 ms per 1080p camera by probe: 0.88 ms copy plus 3.5 ms encode). A start or stop command can wait behind an encode cycle. The loop is also blocked by synchronous pipeline creation (0.25 s sleep per node on Windows), and by SkeletonInferenceNode shutdown joins of up to about 8 s, which the calibration start route triggers right after recording starts. CameraGroup.start_recording and stop_recording also pause the cameras around the transition by design.

Original risk: realtime pipeline throughput is capped by the UI ack rate and stalls with no UI client. Refuted as a general statement. The aggregator's optimistic request has no result_consumed_event gate, so when the pipeline is slower than capture (the 5x60 fps case) it free-runs regardless of the UI. The UI gate applies only when the pipeline outpaces capture. Then requests fall back to the gated bootstrap path, and the pipeline rate drops to the websocket consume rate, or stalls with no client.

Every control/result hop goes child -> mp.Queue -> main-process relay thread (1 ms idle poll) -> mp.Queue -> child, pickled twice. One processed frame needs a ProcessFrameNumber, N CameraNodeOutputs, a SkeletonInferenceResult and an AggregationNodeOutput (which also carries the full pipeline_config), so several milliseconds of relay latency can stack up serially. The relay thread competes for the GIL with the asyncio loop's JPEG work and with the relay's own unpickling of every drained AggregationNodeOutput.

At 1080p the 1 GiB ring holds 172 slots (2.87 s at 60 fps). The staleness check runs only before the copy and is off by one: index = head - (len-1), the slot written next, is accepted. So torn or mismatched reads are possible for a reader at the edge of the window. A CameraNode further behind gets an uncaught IndexError, which is fatal (kill_everything). The UI and skeleton paths tolerate it.

The UI image path does serial per-camera work on one thread at each end. In the main process, all N cameras are JPEG-encoded on the asyncio thread. In the browser, all N are decoded with jpeg-js, synchronously, in a single worker. With 5 cameras that is 5 x (alloc + copy + resize + encode) per UI frame on one Python thread.

Full-resolution copies out of shared memory: 2N per processed multiframe in the default centralized config (N CameraNode copies made even without a tracker, plus N more in the SkeletonInferenceNode for the same frames), plus N per UI frame sent in the main process. Rotations add up to one full-size copy per copy site. On top of this, SkellyCam's writer makes one avoidable extra copy per captured frame (put_data copy(data)).

get_images_by_frame_number allocates a fresh full-frame recarray per camera on every UI payload, because the module cache it checks is never filled. That puts a 5.93 MiB allocation per 1080p camera per UI frame in the main process.
